# Downloads Open Sans from Google Fonts when the poster is rendered, so

# if a render fails while fetching fonts, delete this whole `brand:` block

brand:

format:
  typst:

    citeproc: true
    include-in-header:
      text: |
        // =====================================================================
        //  POSTER SETTINGS  (same options as posterdown_html; edit freely)
        // =====================================================================
        #let poster = (
          width: 45in,
          height: 32in,
          margin: 0.5in,                  // white border around the whole poster (print safety)
          columns: 3,
          column-widths: (1fr, 1.5fr, 1fr),            // e.g. none or (1fr, 1.5fr, 1fr): relative widths, one per

          column-gap: 1em,                // space between columns
          primary: rgb("#0b4545"),        // title bar, section boxes, column lines
          secondary: rgb("#008080"),      // links, code accents
          title-text: white,
          body-text: black,
          font: ("Open Sans", "Segoe UI", "Helvetica Neue", "Noto Sans", "Arial"),  // first one found is used
          body-size: 34pt,                // posterdown: 45px
          title-size: 75pt,
          author-size: 50pt,
          affiliation-size: 35pt,
          sectitle-size: 65pt,
          sectitle-padding: 0.4em,        // colour above and below section heading text (1em = body text size)
          sectitle2-size: 40pt,
          caption-size: 20pt,
          table-row-padding: 10pt,        // space above and below the text in each table row
          hyphenate: false,               // true = split long words across lines with a hyphen
          justify: true,                  // false = ragged right edge (no stretched word gaps)
          list-markers: ([•], [–]),       // bullet shape per level: first, second, ... e.g. [▸], [◦], [–], [·]
          list-spacing: 0.9em,            // space between top-level bullets
          sublist-spacing: 0.5em,         // space between a bullet and its sub-bullets
          titlebox-height: 15%,
          column-line: none, // alternatively:  (thickness: 1mm, dash: (4mm, 3mm)),
          // Logos are set in the `logos` chunk just below the YAML header.
        )

        // =====================================================================
        //  POSTER LAYOUT  (you shouldn't need to edit below this line)
        // =====================================================================
        // {{< pagebreak >}} in the text starts a new column.
        #let pagebreak(..args) = metadata("poster-colbreak")

        #let article(title: none, authors: none, doc, ..rest) = {
          let s = poster
          // Everything is laid out inside the margin: W x H is the printable area
          let W = s.width - 2 * s.margin
          let H = s.height - 2 * s.margin
          let title-h = H * (s.titlebox-height / 100%)
          set page(width: s.width, height: s.height, margin: s.margin, numbering: none)
          set text(font: s.font, size: s.body-size, fill: s.body-text)
          set text(hyphenate: s.hyphenate)
          set par(justify: s.justify, leading: 0.5em, spacing: 0.9em)
          show link: set text(fill: s.secondary)
          show ref: set text(fill: s.secondary)
          show cite: set text(fill: s.secondary)

          // Section headers: filled boxes (#) and plain subheads (##)
          show heading: set text(weight: "regular")
          show heading.where(level: 1): it => block(
            width: 100%, fill: s.primary, sticky: true,
            radius: (top-left: 4mm, bottom-right: 4mm),
            inset: (y: s.sectitle-padding), above: 0.6em, below: 0.5em,
            align(center, text(size: s.sectitle-size, fill: white, it.body)))
          show heading.where(level: 2): it => block(
            sticky: true, inset: (left: 4mm), above: 0.8em, below: 0.4em,
            text(size: s.sectitle2-size, it.body))
          // Bullets: shape per level; sub-bullets sit closer to their parent
          let list-depth = state("poster-list-depth", 0)
          set list(marker: s.list-markers, indent: 4mm, spacing: s.list-spacing)
          show list: it => {
            list-depth.update(d => d + 1)
            context {
              if list-depth.get() > 1 and it.at("spacing", default: auto) != s.sublist-spacing {
                v(s.sublist-spacing - par.spacing)
                let f = it.fields()
                let items = f.remove("children")
                list(..f, spacing: s.sublist-spacing, ..items)
              } else { it }
            }
            list-depth.update(d => d - 1)
          }
          set enum(indent: 4mm)

          // Code
          show raw.where(block: false): it => box(
            fill: s.secondary.lighten(86%), radius: 2mm,
            inset: (x: 1.2mm), outset: (y: 1.5mm),
            text(fill: s.primary, size: 0.85em, it))
          show raw.where(block: true): it => align(center, block(
            width: 85%, fill: none, stroke: 1mm + s.secondary, radius: 0.5em,
            inset: 4mm, breakable: false,
            align(left, {
              set block(fill: none, inset: 0pt, radius: 0pt, width: auto)
              text(size: 20pt, it)
            })))

          // Figures and tables
          show figure: set block(breakable: false, above: 1em, below: 1em)
          show figure.caption: set text(size: s.caption-size)
          set table(inset: (x: 20pt, y: s.table-row-padding), align: center,
            stroke: (x, y) => if y == 0 { (bottom: 3pt + luma(220)) })  // one line under the header row
          show table: it => align(center, box(stroke: (top: 3pt + luma(100), bottom: 3pt + luma(100)), it))
          // Center images (with or without a caption) within the column
          show image: it => block(width: 100%, spacing: 0pt, align(center, it))
          show table: set text(size: 30pt)

          // References list (the {#refs} div)
          show <refs>: set text(size: 22pt)
          show <refs>: set par(justify: false)

          // Title bar
          let affils = ()
          if authors != none {
            for a in authors {
              let af = a.at("affiliation", default: [])
              if af != [] and af not in affils { affils.push(af) }
            }
          }
          // Logo locations come from the `logos` chunk (see below the YAML)
          let logo(side) = context {
            let q = query(label("poster-logo-" + side))
            if q.len() > 0 and q.first().value != none { image(q.first().value, width: 70%) }
          }
          block(width: 100%, height: title-h, fill: s.primary, spacing: 0pt,
            grid(columns: (10%, 80%, 10%), rows: (100%,), align: center + horizon,
              logo("left"),
              text(fill: s.title-text, {
                set par(justify: false)
                if title != none { par(leading: 0.3em, text(size: s.title-size, title)) }
                v(0.2em)
                if authors != none {
                  text(size: s.author-size, authors.map(a => {
                    let af = a.at("affiliation", default: [])
                    let i = affils.position(x => x == af)
                    a.name + if i != none { super(str(i + 1)) }
                  }).join(", "))
                }
                v(0.1em)
                if affils.len() > 0 {
                  text(size: s.affiliation-size, affils.enumerate()
                    .map(((i, af)) => super(str(i + 1)) + " " + af).join("; "))
                }
              }),
              logo("right")))

          // Body: columns with dashed rules between them
          let pad-y = H * 0.01
          let pad-x = 0.5em
          let gap = s.column-gap
          let body-h = H - title-h - 2 * pad-y
          let rule = if s.column-line == none { none } else {
            line(angle: 90deg, length: body-h, stroke: (paint: s.primary) + s.column-line)
          }
          let widths = s.at("column-widths", default: none)
          block(width: 100%, height: H - title-h, spacing: 0pt,
            inset: (x: pad-x, y: pad-y), {
              if widths == none {
                // Equal widths: text flows from one column into the next
                show metadata: it => if it.value == "poster-colbreak" { colbreak() } else { it }
                let n = s.columns
                let colw = (W - 2 * pad-x - (n - 1) * gap) / n
                if rule != none {
                  for i in range(1, n) { place(top + left, dx: i * colw + (i - 0.5) * gap, rule) }
                }
                columns(n, gutter: gap, doc)
              } else {
                // Custom widths: each {{< pagebreak >}} ends a column
                let parts = ((),)
                let kids = if doc.has("children") { doc.children } else { (doc,) }
                for c in kids {
                  if c.func() == metadata and c.value == "poster-colbreak" { parts.push(()) }
                  else { parts.at(-1).push(c) }
                }
                let n = widths.len()
                // Extra pagebreaks beyond the number of columns go into the last column
                while parts.len() > n { let x = parts.pop(); parts.at(-1) += x }
                while parts.len() < n { parts.push(()) }
                let cells = ()
                for (i, p) in parts.enumerate() {
                  if i > 0 { cells.push(align(center, rule)) }
                  cells.push(block(width: 100%, height: body-h, p.join()))
                }
                let cols = ()
                for (i, w) in widths.enumerate() {
                  if i > 0 { cols.push(gap) }
                  cols.push(w)
                }
                grid(columns: cols, ..cells)
              }
            })
        }

```{r}
#| label: logos
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
# ---- Logos ------------------------------------------------------------------
# A GitHub link (".../blob/..." page link or raw link), a path to a local PNG,
# or NA for no logo. Downloads go into Quarto's temporary render folder, which
# is deleted after the PDF is made, so nothing is saved next to this file.

library(tidyverse)

logos <- c(
  left  = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ZoopEcoEvo/lab_utilities/main/lab_logos/text_logo_white.png",
  right = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ZoopEcoEvo/lab_utilities/refs/heads/main/lab_logos/UML_Biology_Logo_White.png"
)

tmp_dir <- dirname(paste0(knitr::opts_chunk$get("fig.path"), "x"))  # Quarto's figure folder
dir.create(tmp_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
token <- Sys.getenv("GITHUB_PAT")

cat("```{=typst}\n")
for (side in names(logos)) {
  src <- gsub("&#58;", ":", logos[[side]], fixed = TRUE)  # undo the visual editor's escaped colon
  path <- NA
  if (!is.na(src) && grepl("^https?://", src)) {
    url  <- sub("^https://github.com/([^/]+/[^/]+)/blob/", "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/\\1/", src)
    dest <- file.path(tmp_dir, paste0("logo-", side, ".png"))
    ok <- tryCatch({
      download.file(url, dest, mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE,
                    headers = if (nzchar(token)) c(Authorization = paste("token", token)))
      identical(readBin(dest, "raw", 4), as.raw(c(0x89, 0x50, 0x4e, 0x47)))  # is it a PNG?
    }, error = function(e) FALSE, warning = function(w) FALSE)
    if (ok) path <- dest else message("Couldn't download ", url, "; leaving the ", side, " logo blank.")
  } else if (!is.na(src)) {
    path <- src  # local file
  }
  cat(sprintf("#metadata(%s) <poster-logo-%s>\n",
              if (is.na(path)) "none" else paste0('"', path, '"'), side))
}
cat("```\n")

```

# Introduction

- Heatwaves are projected to increase in duration and intensity by the end of the century

- Acclimation: Short-term and often reversible change in physiology

  - No genetic change required

- Temporal dynamics of acclimation defined by **capacity** and **rate of acclimation**

```{r acclim-schematic, out.width='100%', fig.align='center', fig.height=4}

acclim <- function(t, t_shift = 0, p0 = 1, capacity = 2, lambda = 0.25) {
  ifelse(t < t_shift,
         p0,
         p0 + capacity * (1 - exp(-lambda * (t - t_shift))))
}

t       <- seq(-6, 30, by = 0.05)
t_shift <- 0
p0      <- 1
cap     <- 2
lambda  <- 0.25
t_half  <- log(2) / lambda
p_half  <- p0 + cap / 2
p_final <- p0 + cap

# Colours
col_main <- "#1b4f72"
col_cap  <- "#c0392b"
col_rate <- "#d68910"
col_env  <- "grey30"

trait_df <- data.frame(time = t, trait = acclim(t, t_shift, p0, cap, lambda))

# Initial tangent: slope = lambda * C, reaches the asymptote at t = 1/lambda
tangent_df <- data.frame(x = t_shift, xend = t_shift + 1 / lambda,
                         y = p0, yend = p_final)

ggplot(trait_df, aes(time, trait)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = t_shift, linetype = "dotted",
             colour = "grey60") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(p0, p_final), linetype = "dashed",
             colour = "grey55") +
  annotate("text", x = -6, y = p0 + 0.12, hjust = 0, size = 3.2,
           label = "Acclimated to env. 1") +
  annotate("text", x = 30, y = p_final + 0.12, hjust = 1, size = 3.2,
           label = "Acclimated to env. 2") +
  geom_segment(data = tangent_df,
               aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y, yend = yend),
               inherit.aes = FALSE, linetype = "longdash",
               colour = col_rate, linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = t_half, xend = t_half, y = p0 - 0.25, yend = p_half),
               linetype = "dotted", colour = col_rate) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = t_shift, xend = t_half, y = p0 - 0.25, yend = p0 - 0.25),
               colour = col_rate,
               arrow = grid::arrow(ends = "both", length = unit(1.5, "mm"))) +
  annotate("point", x = t_half, y = p_half, colour = col_rate, size = 2.5) +
  annotate("text", x = t_half / 2, y = p0 - 0.4, colour = col_rate,
           size = 3.5, label = "t½ = ln(2) / λ") +
  annotate("text", x = t_half + 1.2, y = p_half - 0.05, hjust = 0,
           colour = col_rate, size = 3.5, fontface = "bold",
           label = "Rate of acclimation (λ)") +
    annotate("segment", x = 27, xend = 27, y = p0, yend = p_final,
           colour = col_cap, linewidth = 0.8,
           arrow = grid::arrow(ends = "both", length = unit(2, "mm"))) +
  annotate("text", x = 27 - 0.6, y = p_half, hjust = 1,
           colour = col_cap, size = 3.5, fontface = "bold",
           label = "Capacity for\nacclimation (C)") +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1.2, colour = col_main) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(p0 - 0.55, p_final + 0.3)) +
  labs(x = "Time since environmental change",
       y = "Physiological trait") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 18) +
  theme(
    axis.text  = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks = element_blank(),
    axis.line  = element_line(arrow = grid::arrow(length = unit(2, "mm"),
                                                  type = "closed")),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_blank()
  )

```

- Minimal information on how these parameters vary across populations

\

# Central Question

Do acclimation parameters vary across populations?

\

## **Hypotheses**

1\. The acclimation capacity will be higher in the population with a higher average surface temperature.

2\. The acclimation capacity and rate of acclimation will have a negative relationship.

# Results

```{r message = F, warning = F, echo=F}

ctmax_data = read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ZoopEcoEvo/Skisto_LARA/refs/heads/main/Output/Output_data/ctmax_data.csv")

acc_params = read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ZoopEcoEvo/Skisto_LARA/refs/heads/main/Output/Output_data/acc_params.csv")

contrasts = read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ZoopEcoEvo/Skisto_LARA/refs/heads/main/Output/Output_data/contrasts.csv")

library(tidyverse)

```

```{r ctmax-plot, out.width='90%', fig.align='center', fig.cap='CTmax (°C) over time (Acclimation hours) for the control (blue) and warming (red) treatments. The two populations are shown separately. Each point represents an individual copepods upper thermal limit. Logistic regressions are fit to each treatment group.', fig.height=4.1}


ctmax_data %>% 
  filter(ctmax > 34) %>% 
  mutate(acc_hours = acc_hours + 0.1) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = acc_hours, y = ctmax, colour = treatment)) + 
  facet_wrap(pop ~ .) +
  geom_point(size = 2) + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ log(x)) + 
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("control" = "royalblue",
                                 "warming" = "brown2")) + 
  labs(
    x = "Acclimation Hour", 
    y = "CTmax (°C)"
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 18) + 
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom", 
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  )
```

```{r contrast-plot, out.width='90%', fig.align='center', fig.cap='Plot of the model contrasts (Warming - Control; °C) over time (Acclimation Day) for the two populations. The blue lines indicate the fitted acclimation equation based on the rate and capacity parameters.', fig.height=3.35}

param_data = contrasts %>%
  group_by(pop) %>% 
  arrange(acc_day) %>% 
  mutate(acc_day = if_else(acc_day == 0, 0.01, acc_day)) 

cp_params = filter(acc_params, pop == "CP")
op_params = filter(acc_params, pop == "OP")

# Create a new data frame with predicted values
acc_day <- seq(0, max(param_data$acc_day), length.out = 100)
cp_pred <- cp_params$z_asymp*(1-exp(-cp_params$lambda*acc_day))
op_pred <- op_params$z_asymp*(1-exp(-op_params$lambda*acc_day))

predictions = data.frame(acc_day, 
                         cp_pred, 
                         op_pred) %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = c(cp_pred:op_pred), 
               names_to = c("pop", NA), 
               names_sep = "_", 
               values_to = "pred") %>% 
  mutate(pop = toupper(pop))

param_data %>% 
  drop_na(estimate) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = acc_day, y = estimate)) + 
  facet_wrap(pop~.) + 
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0) +
  geom_hline(data = acc_params, aes(yintercept = z_asymp),
             colour = "grey") + 
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = estimate - SE, ymax = estimate + SE), 
                linewidth = 1, width = 0.3) + 
  geom_point(size = 3) + 
  geom_line(data = predictions, aes(x = acc_day, y = pred),
            colour = "blue",
            linewidth=1.5)+
  labs(x = "Acc. Day", 
       y = "Change in CTmax (°C)") + 
  theme_bw(base_size = 18) + 
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), 
        legend.position = "bottom")

```

# Methods

![](exp_design.png){fig-align="center"}

# Conclusions

- *S. pallidus* is able to acclimate rapidly to warming.

- Populations differ in both capacity and acclimation, with a potental negative correlation between capacity and rate of acclimation.

# Next Steps

- Replicate with additional populations of *S. pallidus*
